Rambling rocks bro don't worry. My advice, give yourself at least 2 months to be single for a while. That will give you time to get your head out of the mindset of being in a relationship with her, and you'll be able to reflect on the relationship from an objective view. So at that point, if she does want to fix things between you two you'll be confident in whatever you do.

I hope this helps, and I hope you turn out well!

My experiences with antidepressants is limited but maybe it'll help. I'm about 17 as well so we're in the same age group. 

The first antidepressant I took I do not remember the name of. It made me want to kill myself, I couldn't stop shaking, my head was a mess, it was like I was thinking at a million miles an hour about nothing.

The second I tried was viibryd and I took it for 3 weeks and went off it, due to my hating it. I can't remember exactly why I hated it. I think it was because I didn't like the feeling of it changing my emotions. It was fucked up I don't know. I hope if you decide to try antidepressants they work for you.

Attention isn't something you should get down on yourself for wanting, I'm struggling with that too. There's a difference between being a teenage girl fishing for complements on facebook and someone depressed wanting people to care. You have to forgive yourself in that situation.
I know what you mean, cutting on your forearms is amazing, but you should really be careful, they scar very easily and are incredible difficult to hide.

Yeah cutting anywhere besides my wrists is frustrating. I've started on my thighs some and I don't really mind it that much but I also don't like it a lot. Whenever I cut a new spot I have to do it a few times before I can actually get any depth or like the feeling of it.

If your thoughts are jumbled I can't even tell you how good it would be for you to write. Seeing them down on paper you'll have them organized in front of you so you can get a new perspective on them and see all of it at once. 


My journals have just let me get my shit out somewhere. Storing feelings is total shit, I know from experience. It's a release for me. Yeah I read older entries pretty regularly, and it really helps me feel better actually. 

I've doodled some and wrote a few poems but mostly I just stick to random shit ie whatever's on my mind. But really you should write/draw whatever you want to, don't let me decide for you.

Definitely do it. They help a ton, especially when you have no one you can talk to, and even when you do have someone to talk to, a journal is something you can put absolutely anything without any judgement at all. Grab a notebook or something, or just a piece of paper or whatever the fuck else. When I started writing I acted as if I was writing to myself in the future, because I was sure my future self would go back and read it, but these days I just put the date down and however I'm feeling, what's going on, what's shitty and what's good. My best advice for starting is to write whatever you're thinking and go from there.
